transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (CIO - Valley First), Sofia Martinez (Head of Compliance), Derek Huang (Cloud Architect)

Summary: (auto) Quick discovery focused on data residency, regulatory scope (financial services), and options between Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployment. Customer is concerned about logs, audit trails, KMS/HSM, and GDPR/HIPAA overlap for certain products. They want a technical architecture sketch for VPC/private and an initial pricing ballpark and a Dedicated throughput benchmark in their region.

Topics: data residency, VPC/Private deployment, SOC2/HIPAA, KMS/HSM, audit logs, logging retention & redaction, RBAC/SSO, network egress, model routing, fallback policies

Transcript:
[14:30] Evan Brooks: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Evan from Redwood, that's Priya on the call from our solution engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[14:31] Mark Reynolds: Good, thanks. We've been evaluating a few options, want to understand how Redwood handles data residency and what options we have between hosted, dedicated and private.
[14:31] Evan Brooks: Totally. Priya will jump into the technical bits, but high level: hosted is fastest to get started, dedicated gives reserved capacity and better isolation, and private gives you control of the control plane and networking - VPC or on-prem.
[14:32] Priya Desai: Hi all. Can I ask a few quick qualifiers? What workloads are you planning - PII customer support, loan origination, internal docs search? Any PHI/PD or regulated data?
[14:32] Sofia Martinez: Some of our consumer loan forms include health-related disclosures in a tiny subset - so potentially HIPAA overlap in rare cases. Mostly financial PII, account numbers, SSNs, stuff like that. We also have EU customers so GDPR is in scope for parts of our data.
[14:33] Priya Desai: Understood. For HIPAA and strict financial controls we typically recommend private or dedicated depending on throughput and timeline. Hosted can work if you have contractual controls, but many banks prefer dedicated or private because of audit requirements and log residency.
[14:34] Derek Huang: Can you clarify what you mean by "log residency"? We need logs to stay in our region and be subject to our retention policies. Also redaction - our legal team will not accept raw transcripts stored outside our environment.
[14:34] Priya Desai: Sure. For dedicated deployments we can configure logging to ship to your logging endpoint in-region, and we offer options to disable storing full transcripts in Redwood's hosted storage. For private (VPC) deployments the control plane and logs can be inside your VPC or on-prem, so you own the storage. We also support redaction and can run a near-real-time filter to remove PII before it's persisted.
[14:35] Evan Brooks: To add - our Dedicated customers can opt for log forwarding to customer-managed S3 or Splunk in their region; we also support sending audit logs to their KMS-protected storage so keys never leave their account.
[14:36] Mark Reynolds: How about encryption key management - KMS or HSM? Our policy requires keys to be under our control, ideally HSM-backed.
[14:36] Priya Desai: We integrate with customer KMS providers; for private deployments you can bring your own key material and HSM if you run on-prem. For Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS in supported cloud providers - keys in your account and we use envelope encryption. For hosted, we offer a managed KMS but can support customer-managed keys for enterprise customers under an agreement.
[14:37] Sofia Martinez: What about auditability - we need detailed audit logs for who queried what model, which model version, and the raw request IDs, plus chain of custody.
[14:37] Priya Desai: We emit per-request audit logs with model id, model version, route, user id and request timestamp. For Private deployment, these logs are written to your sinks. For Dedicated, we retain logs for the contractually agreed retention and can forward them. We can also redact request bodies on write, or redact sensitive fields via config.
[14:38] Derek Huang: Any limit on redaction - like do you support regex-based PII redaction or structured field scrubbing?
[14:38] Priya Desai: Both - simple regex redactors, plus structured scrubbing for JSON inputs. For more complex workflows we can chain a pre-processing step in your VPC to run advanced redaction before hitting the model. That option is common in Private deployments.
[14:39] Mark Reynolds: From a compliance standpoint, we need SOC 2, ISO, HIPAA BAAs etc. Do you have those?
[14:39] Evan Brooks: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and can provide our reports; HIPAA support is available and we sign BAAs for customers with covered workloads. I'll attach the certs and the legal BAA text.
[14:40] Sofia Martinez: Are there any known gaps we should be aware of for European residency? We can't have EEA customer data leave the region without consent.
[14:40] Priya Desai: For EU data we can pin inference to an EU region node for both Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can request region locking; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in the customer's cloud region or a Private VPC in your EU environment. There are compliance controls around backups and logs too - we can ensure backups are region-restricted for private deployments.
[14:41] Derek Huang: Performance/latency is also a factor. If we do a private on-prem deployment, what are the tradeoffs compared to Redwood hosted?
[14:41] Priya Desai: On-prem gives you ultimate control but you are responsible for hardware sizing and patching. Our runtime is optimized for GPUs; we provide guidance on kernel selection and batching. Dedicated gives you the benefits of managed infra with reserved capacity and SLAs - lower ops burden than full on-prem. Hosted is easiest but may not meet strict residency or key custody needs.
[14:42] Evan Brooks: Also, our smart routing and fallback policies can route to cheaper model variants if capacity is limited; we can preserve latency SLOs with caching, but dedicated/private deployments let you avoid cross-region network hops.
[14:42] Mark Reynolds: Regarding logs again - our legal will not accept full content logs being stored outside our control. Is it possible to have no-content logs retained by Redwood, only metadata?
[14:43] Priya Desai: Yes, we have a no-content logging mode that captures metadata only (timestamps, model/version, request IDs, latency). For Dedicated we can enable that and forward any raw content to your sinks if you require. For hosted, we can enable contractual controls and limited retention windows.
[14:44] Sofia Martinez: Can you talk about deletion and data retention? We need to be able to delete PII on request and have retention windows aligned with our policy.
[14:44] Priya Desai: For private deployments you control retention. For Dedicated and hosted we offer retention configuration and end-to-end deletion APIs - we can run deletions and provide attestations. For GDPR right-to-erasure, we can assist with mapping request IDs to persisted artifacts.
[14:45] Derek Huang: Is there support for SSO/SAML and RBAC so we can integrate with our corporate directory?
[14:45] Evan Brooks: Yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning for users and role-based access controls. We can restrict access to routes/models by role and provide token scoping so only certain tokens can invoke specific models.
[14:46] Mark Reynolds: Anything we should flag for procurement/legal - contracts, indemnities, export controls?
[14:46] Evan Brooks: We'll share our standard enterprise contract and BAA. Export controls are typically handled in the agreement; we can add clauses for data residency and for any special audit requirements.
[14:47] Priya Desai: One practical note: if you need model weights never to leave your environment (no replication), Private on-prem is the only way to guarantee that. Dedicated is isolated but we still manage the infra.
[14:48] Sofia Martinez: For the workloads we plan, we're leaning toward Dedicated in our EU and US regions for latency+control, and Private for the most sensitive flows. It's probably a hybrid approach.
[14:48] Evan Brooks: That's a common pattern - Dedicated for customer-facing features, Private for internal or high-risk pipelines. We can help with the rollout plan and A/B model routing during migration.
[14:49] Derek Huang: Can we run an initial throughput benchmark? We want to validate p99 latency under a production-like burst pattern.
[14:49] Priya Desai: Absolutely. We'll schedule a Dedicated benchmark in your region - we'll need a sample workload, target sequence lengths, and concurrency profile. I'll follow up with a template.
[14:50] Mark Reynolds: Cost is the main objection internally - our finance team will push back on reserved spend for Dedicated. Can you provide modeling on batching and caching benefits to show unit cost?
[14:50] Evan Brooks: Yes, Redwood Optimize can provide workload-specific recommendations and cost modeling; we'll include quantization and batching profiles in the estimate.
[14:51] Sofia Martinez: Any concerns about third-party models and licensing for EU data?
[14:51] Priya Desai: We track model licensing; for private deployments you control which models are onboarded. For hosted/dedicated we can provide a model catalog with licensing notes. We can also pin model versions for reproducibility and audits.
[14:52] Mark Reynolds: Great. Let's confirm immediate next steps.
[14:52] Evan Brooks: Recap: I'll send SOC2/HIPAA/BAA docs and pricing ballpark; Priya will draft a VPC/private architecture and a benchmark template; Derek will share infra/network diagrams and compliance checklist. We'll schedule the Dedicated benchmark and a follow-up meeting next week.
[14:53] Sofia Martinez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[14:54] Evan Brooks: Thanks all, we'll follow up by email with attachments and a calendar invite.

End of transcript.
